_comment: Source of truth for the command builder page (docs/index.html, served by GitHub Pages from the docs/ folder of main). Facts only — the wiring logic lives in docs/builder/app.js and references entries here by id. Keep this file in sync with entrypoint.sh, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml and wiki/Docker.md; scripts/ci/validate_command_builder.sh cross-checks a few key values on every CI build.

flavors.label: Full
flavors.summary: Scraper + AceStream engine + Acexy proxy in one container. Pick this if you are not sure.

flavors.label: Scraper + engine
flavors.summary: Scraper with the AceStream engine, no Acexy proxy.

flavors.label: Scraper + Acexy
flavors.summary: Scraper with the Acexy proxy; the AceStream engine runs somewhere else.

flavors.label: Scraper only
flavors.summary: Just the scraper and web interface. Engine and proxy, if any, run somewhere else.

platforms.label: x86_64 / amd64
platforms.summary: Regular PCs, servers, NAS with Intel/AMD CPUs.

platforms.label: ARM 64-bit
platforms.summary: Raspberry Pi 4/5 (64-bit OS), most ARM servers.
platforms.engine: Android engine 3.2.17 on a bionic userland

platforms.label: ARM 32-bit
platforms.summary: Older ARM boards running a 32-bit OS.
platforms.engine: Android engine 3.1.80 on a bionic userland

ports.label: Web interface
ports.description: The scraper's web UI and API (uvicorn, port set by FLASK_PORT).

ports.label: Acexy proxy
ports.description: Stream endpoint used by your players: http://<server>:<port>/ace/getstream?id=<channel id>.

ports.label: Engine HTTP API
ports.description: The AceStream engine's HTTP API. Only needed if players or other machines talk to the engine directly.
ports.securityNote: The engine API has no authentication — only publish it on trusted networks.

ports.label: P2P port
ports.description: The engine's peer-to-peer port (TCP and UDP). Publishing it improves peer connectivity.

ports.label: IPFS swarm
ports.description: The embedded IPFS node's peer-to-peer port (TCP and UDP/QUIC, IPFS_SWARM_PORT). Publishing it improves peer connectivity.

ports.label: IPFS gateway
ports.description: The embedded node's HTTP gateway (IPFS_GATEWAY_PORT; 8081 in-container because Acexy owns 8080). The scraper reaches it internally — publish it only if you want to browse IPFS content through this node.
ports.securityNote: The IPFS RPC API on port 5001 is not offered here on purpose: it is unauthenticated and controls the whole node. If you need the WebUI, bind it to the host's loopback only (see the Docker guide).

ports.label: ZeroNet UI
ports.description: The bundled node's web interface (ZERONET_UI_PORT). The scraper reaches it internally — publish it only to browse ZeroNet yourself, and set ZERONET_UI_HOST so it accepts your hostname.
ports.securityNote: The ZeroNet UI has no authentication and full control of the node — only publish it on trusted networks.

ports.label: ZeroNet fileserver
ports.description: The bundled node's peer/fileserver port (ZERONET_FILESERVER_PORT). Publishing it improves peer connectivity.

volumes.label: Configuration & database
volumes.description: Holds the SQLite database and runtime config. Without it your channels and settings are lost when the container is replaced.

volumes.label: Engine state & cache
volumes.description: Engine state, disk cache and logs (ACESTREAM_HOME). Used by the Android engine on ARM; harmless on amd64.

volumes.label: IPFS repository
volumes.description: Node identity, config and blockstore of the embedded IPFS daemon (IPFS_PATH). Without it the node re-initializes with a new identity on every container replacement.

volumes.label: ZeroNet node state
volumes.description: Sites, keys and content of the bundled ZeroNet node (ZERONET_DATA_DIR). Without it the node re-downloads everything on every container replacement.

zeronet.description: Scrape zero:// sources. The amd64 images bundle a ZeroNet node (opt-in via ENABLE_ZERONET), or point ZERONET_URL at an external ZeroNet service.
zeronet.embeddedDescription: Starts the bundled zeronet-conservancy node; zero:// sources are fetched through its UI port (43110). Turn off to use an external ZeroNet service instead.

ipfs.description: Scrape ipfs:// and ipns:// sources. Every image bundles the Kubo daemon on amd64/arm64 (opt-in via ENABLE_IPFS), or point IPFS_GATEWAY_URL at an external IPFS gateway.
ipfs.embeddedDescription: Starts the bundled Kubo daemon; ipfs:// sources are fetched through its gateway on 8081 (8080 belongs to Acexy). Turn off to use an external gateway instead.

notes.developChannel: The develop tags are moving pre-release builds meant for testing the next release — not for production.
notes.armv7Experimental: The 32-bit ARM engine builds and installs but has not been runtime-tested on real hardware. Prefer a 64-bit OS where the device supports it.
notes.armPageSize: The Android engine needs a 4 KB kernel page size. On Raspberry Pi 5 (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit) set kernel=kernel8.img in config.txt — the default kernel uses 16 KB pages and the engine refuses to start.
notes.warpArm: The WARP client (cloudflare-warp) is amd64-only; ARM images ship without it.
notes.ipfsArmv7: Kubo publishes no 32-bit ARM build, so 32-bit ARM images ship without the embedded IPFS daemon. IPFS sources still work through an external gateway (IPFS_GATEWAY_URL).
notes.zeronetArm: The bundled ZeroNet node ships in the amd64 images only. ZeroNet sources still work through an external service (ZERONET_URL).
notes.warpCaps: WARP needs the NET_ADMIN and SYS_ADMIN capabilities.
notes.acexyExternalEngine: Acexy refuses to start against localhost:6878 when the in-container engine is disabled — point it at your external engine's address.
notes.externalEngineSettings: The scraper's own engine connection (used for channel status checks) is configured in the web interface under Settings → Acestream Engine URL.
notes.afterRun: Then open http://localhost:{webPort} — set the stream base URL and engine URL under Settings, and add source URLs under Scraper.
